fr.title: [Marketing 101 #4] Pourquoi vous vous tourmentez pendant trois semaines pour des chaussures de course et trois secondes pour un chewing-gum

segments.src: > Four forces decide what you buy — how much you care (involvement), what need is driving you (motivation), what you already believe (attitude), and who you're secretly buying for (reference groups).
segments.tr: > Quatre forces décident de ce que vous achetez — l'importance que vous y accordez (implication), le besoin qui vous pousse (motivation), ce que vous croyez déjà (attitude) et pour qui vous achetez en secret (groupes de référence).

segments.src: ## Today's Concept
segments.tr: ## Concept du jour

segments.src: Most of us think we shop rationally: compare options, pick the best one, done.
segments.tr: La plupart d'entre nous pensons que nous achetons de manière rationnelle : comparer les options, choisir la meilleure, c'est fait.

segments.src: In reality, the amount of thinking you do varies wildly from purchase to purchase — and it's fairly predictable.
segments.tr: En réalité, la quantité de réflexion que vous y mettez varie énormément d'un achat à l'autre — et c'est assez prévisible.

segments.src: Consumer behavior researchers explain that variation with four building blocks.
segments.tr: Les chercheurs en comportement du consommateur expliquent cette variation à l'aide de quatre piliers.

segments.src: Involvement — how much this purchase matters to you.**
segments.tr: Implication — l'importance de cet achat pour vous.**

segments.src: Involvement is the personal relevance of a purchase, and it rises with the perceived risk: money at stake, how visible the choice is to other people, how long you're stuck with it, and how bad it feels to get it wrong.
segments.tr: L'implication est la pertinence personnelle d'un achat, et elle augmente avec le risque perçu : l'argent en jeu, la visibilité du choix pour les autres, la durée pendant laquelle vous le conservez et le sentiment désagréable de vous tromper.

segments.src: High involvement means an extended decision process — research, spreadsheets, reviews, second opinions.
segments.tr: Une forte implication signifie un processus de décision prolongé : recherches, tableurs, avis, seconds avis.

segments.src: Low involvement means habit or impulse: you grab the familiar package and move on.
segments.tr: Une faible implication signifie une habitude ou une impulsion : vous saisissez l'emballage familier et vous passez à autre situ.

segments.src: Same shopper, same day, completely different behavior.
segments.tr: Même acheteur, même jour, comportement complètement différent.

segments.src: Note that involvement is a property of the *situation*, not just the product: a $4 coffee is low involvement on a Tuesday and high involvement when you're buying it for a first date.
segments.tr: Notez que l'implication est une propriété de la *situation*, pas seulement du produit : un café à 4 $ est une faible implication un mardi et une forte implication lorsque vous l'achetez pour un premier rendez-vous.

segments.src: Motivation — the tension that gets you moving.**
segments.tr: Motivation — la tension qui vous met en mouvement.**

segments.src: Motivation is an activated need: a gap between where you are and where you want to be, strong enough to push you toward action.
segments.tr: La motivation est un besoin activé : un fossé entre là où vous êtes et là où vous voulez être, assez fort pour vous pousser vers l'action.

segments.src: Two flavors usually run at once:
segments.tr: Deux saveurs fonctionnent généralement en même temps :

segments.src: - *Utilitarian* motives — solve the problem. Keep my feet from hurting. Get the laundry clean.
segments.tr: - Motifs *utilitaires* — résoudre le problème. Empêcher mes pieds d'avoir mal. Faire la lessive.

segments.src: - *Hedonic* motives — feel something. Look like the kind of person who runs. Enjoy the unboxing.
segments.tr: - Motifs *hédoniques* — ressentir quelque chose. Avoir l'air du genre de personne qui court. Apprécier le déballage.

segments.src: Buyers rarely admit the second one out loud, which is exactly why survey answers and actual receipts often disagree.
segments.tr: Les acheteurs admettent rarement le deuxième à voix haute, c'est exactement pourquoi les réponses aux sondages et les reçus réels sont souvent en désaccord.

segments.src: Motives also conflict: wanting the upgrade *and* not wanting the bill (approach–avoidance) is why "0% APR for 12 months" closes so many sales — it doesn't change the price, it defuses the avoidance side.
segments.tr: Les motifs entrent également en conflit : vouloir la mise à niveau *et* ne pas vouloir la facture (approche-évitement) explique pourquoi "0 % TAEG pendant 12 mois" conclut tant de ventes — cela ne change pas le prix, cela désamorce le côté évitement.

segments.src: Attitude — the stored verdict you carry around.**
segments.tr: Attitude — le verdict stocké que vous transportez partout.**

segments.src: An attitude is a learned, reasonably stable tendency to respond favorably or unfavorably to something.
segments.tr: Une attitude est une tendance apprise et raisonnablement stable à réagir favorablement ou défavorablement à quelque chose.

segments.src: The classic model has three parts, often called ABC:
segments.tr: Le modèle classique comporte trois parties, souvent appelées ABC :

segments.src: - **Affect** — how you feel about it ("Patagonia feels honest")
segments.tr: - **Affect** — ce que vous ressentez à ce sujet (« Patagonia semble honnête »)

segments.src: - **Behavior** — what you intend to do ("I'd buy it next time")
segments.tr: - **Comportement** — ce que vous avez l'intention de faire (« Je l'achèterais la prochaine fois »)

segments.src: - **Cognition** — what you believe about it ("their gear lasts a decade")
segments.tr: - **Cognition** — ce que vous croyez à son sujet (« leur équipement dure une décennie »)

segments.src: A useful working model is the multiattribute view: your overall attitude is roughly the sum of what you believe about each attribute, weighted by how much that attribute matters to you.
segments.tr: Un modèle de travail utile est la vue multi-attributs : votre attitude globale est à peu près la somme de ce que vous croyez de chaque attribut, pondérée par l'importance de cet attribut pour vous.

segments.src: Attitude ≈ sum of (belief about attribute) × (importance of that attribute)
segments.tr: Attitude ≈ sum of (belief about attribute) × (importance of that attribute)

segments.src: That equation quietly explains most marketing tactics.
segments.tr: Cette équation explique discrètement la plupart des tactiques marketing.

segments.src: If people rate you low on an attribute, you can change the belief ("actually, we're 30% lighter").
segments.tr: Si les gens vous évaluent bas sur un attribut, vous pouvez changer la croyance (« en fait, nous sommes 30 % plus légers »).

segments.src: Or change the weight ("weight isn't what causes injuries — cushioning is").
segments.tr: Ou changer le poids (« le poids ne cause pas les blessures — c'est l'amorti »).

segments.src: Or add a brand-new attribute nobody was scoring yet ("carbon plate").
segments.tr: Ou ajouter un tout nouvel attribut que personne ne notait encore (« plaque en carbone »).

segments.src: Changing what people care about is often cheaper than changing what they believe.
segments.tr: Changer ce qui importe aux gens est souvent moins cher que de changer ce qu'ils croient.

segments.src: Reference groups — the invisible audience.**
segments.tr: Groupes de référence — le public invisible.**

segments.src: A reference group is any set of people you use as a benchmark for your own beliefs and behavior.
segments.tr: Un groupe de référence est tout ensemble de personnes que vous utilisez comme point de repère pour vos propres croyances et comportements.

segments.src: Three types matter: **membership** groups you actually belong to, **aspirational** groups you'd like to join, and **dissociative** groups you actively want to avoid resembling.
segments.tr: Trois types comptent : les groupes d'**appartenance** auxquels vous appartenez réellement, les groupes **d'aspiration** que vous aimeriez rejoindre et les groupes **dissociatifs** que vous voulez activement éviter de ressembler.

segments.src: They influence you two ways: **normative** ("buy this or you won't fit in") and **informational** ("these people know things I don't, so I'll copy them").
segments.tr: Ils vous influencent de deux manières : **normative** (« achetez ceci ou vous ne vous intégrerez pas ») et **informationnelle** (« ces gens savent des choses que je ne sais pas, donc je vais les copier »).

segments.src: The practical rule researchers have found repeatedly: reference groups exert the most pull on things that are **publicly visible and non-essential** — the car in the driveway, the water bottle on your desk.
segments.tr: La règle pratique que les chercheurs ont trouvée à maintes reprises : les groupes de référence exercent le plus d'attraction sur les choses qui sont **visiblement publiques et non essentielles** — la voiture dans l'allée, la bouteille d'eau sur votre bureau.

segments.src: They exert the least pull on private necessities.
segments.tr: Ils exercent le moins d'attraction sur les nécessités privées.

segments.src: Nobody chooses a mattress to impress the neighbors.
segments.tr: Personne ne choisit un matelas pour impressionner les voisins.

segments.src: ## In Everyday Life
segments.tr: ## Dans la vie de tous les jours

segments.src: Say you live in Columbus and you just signed up for your first half marathon in October.
segments.tr: Disons que vous vivez à Columbus et que vous venez de vous inscrire à votre premier semi-marathon en octobre.

segments.src: Here's all four forces in one shopping trip.
segments.tr: Voici les quatre forces en un seul voyage de shopping.

segments.src: **Motivation** shows up as two needs at once.
segments.tr: La **motivation** apparaît comme deux besoins à la fois.

segments.src: Utilitarian: your knees ache after three miles in old sneakers.
segments.tr: Utilitaire : vos genoux vous font mal après trois miles dans de vieilles baskets.

segments.src: Hedonic: you want to *be a runner*, not someone who owns running shoes.
segments.tr: Hédonique : vous voulez *être un coureur*, pas quelqu'un qui possède des chaussures de course.

segments.src: Both are real; only the first one comes out of your mouth at the store.
segments.tr: Les deux sont réels ; seul le premier sort de votre bouche au magasin.

segments.src: **Involvement** spikes.
segments.tr: L'**implication** grimpe en flèche.

segments.src: This is a $165 purchase you'll wear for 400 miles, and picking wrong means shin splints in September.
segments.tr: C'est un achat de 165 $ que vous porterez pendant 400 miles, et un mauvais choix signifie des périostites tibiales en septembre.

segments.src: So you do things you'd never do for socks: you read 40 minutes of reviews, watch two YouTube comparisons, and drive to a specialty shop to get your gait analyzed.
segments.tr: Vous faites donc des choses que vous ne feriez jamais pour des chaussettes : vous lisez 40 minutes de critiques, regardez deux comparaisons YouTube et conduisez jusqu'à une boutique spécialisée pour faire analyser votre foulée.

segments.src: That's extended problem solving.
segments.tr: C'est la résolution de problèmes élargie.

segments.src: Meanwhile you grab a $2 Gatorade at the register without a single conscious thought — same shopper, low involvement, pure habit.
segments.tr: Pendant ce temps, vous attrapez un Gatorade à 2 $ à la caisse sans une seule pensée consciente — même acheteur, faible implication, pure habitude.

segments.src: **Attitude** is what you walk in with.
segments.tr: L'**attitude** est ce avec quoi vous entrez.

segments.src: You already believe Brooks is "reliable but boring," Hoka is "cushioned but ugly," On is "trendy but pricey."
segments.tr: Vous croyez déjà que Brooks est « fiable mais ennuyeux », Hoka est « coussiné mais moche », On est « tendance mais cher ».

segments.src: Those beliefs came from ads, a coworker, and a podcast — not from ever wearing the shoes.
segments.tr: Ces croyances proviennent de publicités, d'un collègue et d'un podcast — pas du fait d'avoir jamais porté les chaussures.

segments.src: Now watch the salesperson work the equation: "Everyone worries about weight, but for a first half, cushioning is what saves your knees."
segments.tr: Regardez maintenant le vendeur travailler l'équation : « Tout le monde s'inquiète du poids, mais pour un premier semi, l'amorti est ce qui sauve vos genoux. »

segments.src: He didn't argue with your beliefs.
segments.tr: Il n'a pas débattu avec vos croyances.

segments.src: He reweighted the attributes, and suddenly the Hokas look smart.
segments.tr: Il a repondéré les attributs, et soudain les Hoka ont l'air intelligentes.

segments.src: **Reference groups** close the deal.
segments.tr: Les **groupes de référence** concluent l'affaire.

segments.src: The Saturday morning run club you just joined is a membership group — you notice half of them wear the same shoe and you feel the pull to match (normative), and you also assume they know things you don't (informational).
segments.tr: Le club de course du samedi matin que vous venez de rejoindre est un groupe d'appartenance — vous remarquez que la moitié d'entre eux portent la même chaussure et vous ressentez l'attraction d'assortir (normative), et vous supposez également qu'ils savent des choses que vous ignorez (informationnelle).

segments.src: The guy who ran Boston is your aspirational group; the Strava thread is a running commentary of both.
segments.tr: Le gars qui a couru Boston est votre groupe d'aspiration ; le fil de discussion Strava est un commentaire courant des deux.

segments.src: And the shoes are highly visible and entirely optional — the exact conditions where reference group influence is strongest.
segments.tr: Et les chaussures sont très visibles et entièrement optionnelles — les conditions exactes où l'influence du groupe de référence est la plus forte.

segments.src: Your mattress, bought last spring, got none of this energy at all.
segments.tr: Votre matelas, acheté le printemps dernier, n'a reçu aucune de cette énergie.

segments.src: ## Three-Line Recap
segments.tr: ## Récapitulatif en trois lignes

segments.src: 1. **Involvement** decides how much thinking a purchase gets — driven by perceived risk (money, visibility, permanence), and it's situational, not just product-based.
segments.tr: 1. L'**implication** décide de la quantité de réflexion qu'un achat reçoit — motivée par le risque perçu (argent, visibilité, permanence), et elle est situationnelle, pas seulement basée sur le produit.

segments.src: 2. **Motivation** is the activated need pushing you forward, and it's usually utilitarian and hedonic at once; **attitude** is your stored verdict, roughly beliefs weighted by importance — which is why reweighting attributes is a marketer's cheapest lever.
segments.tr: 2. La **motivation** est le besoin activé qui vous pousse vers l'avant, et elle est généralement utilitaire et hédonique à la fois ; l'**attitude** est votre verdict stocké, à peu près des croyances pondérées par l'importance — c'est pourquoi repondérer les attributs est le levier le moins cher d'un spécialiste du marketing.

segments.src: 3. **Reference groups** shape choices most powerfully when the product is publicly visible and non-essential, through normative (fit in) and informational (they know better) influence.
segments.tr: 3. Les **groupes de référence** façonnent les choix le plus puissamment lorsque le produit est visible publiquement et non essentiel, par le biais d'une influence normative (s'intégrer) et informationnelle (ils en savent plus).

segments.src: > Four forces decide what you buy — how much you care (involvement), what need is driving you (motivation), what you already believe (attitude), and who you're secretly buying for (reference groups).
segments.tr: > Quatro forças decidem o que você compra — quanto você se importa (envolvimento), qual necessidade te impulsiona (motivação), o que você já acredita (atitude) e para quem você está comprando em segredo (grupos de referência).

segments.src: ## Today's Concept
segments.tr: ## Conceito de Hoje

segments.src: Most of us think we shop rationally: compare options, pick the best one, done.
segments.tr: A maioria de nós pensa que faz compras racionalmente: compara opções, escolhe a melhor, pronto.

segments.src: In reality, the amount of thinking you do varies wildly from purchase to purchase — and it's fairly predictable.
segments.tr: Na realidade, a quantidade de pensamento que você tem varia muito de compra para compra — e isso é bastante previsível.

segments.src: Consumer behavior researchers explain that variation with four building blocks.
segments.tr: Pesquisadores de comportamento do consumidor explicam essa variação com quatro blocos de construção.

segments.src: Involvement — how much this purchase matters to you.**
segments.tr: Envolvimento — o quanto essa compra importa para você.**

segments.src: Involvement is the personal relevance of a purchase, and it rises with the perceived risk: money at stake, how visible the choice is to other people, how long you're stuck with it, and how bad it feels to get it wrong.
segments.tr: Envolvimento é a relevância pessoal de uma compra, e ele aumenta com o risco percebido: dinheiro em jogo, quão visível a escolha é para outras pessoas, quanto tempo você fica preso a ela e quão ruim é errar.

segments.src: High involvement means an extended decision process — research, spreadsheets, reviews, second opinions.
segments.tr: Alto envolvimento significa um processo de decisão prolongado — pesquisa, planilhas, avaliações, segundas opiniões.

segments.src: Low involvement means habit or impulse: you grab the familiar package and move on.
segments.tr: Baixo envolvimento significa hábito ou impulso: você pega a embalagem familiar e segue em frente.

segments.src: Same shopper, same day, completely different behavior.
segments.tr: Mesmo comprador, mesmo dia, comportamento completamente diferente.

segments.src: Note that involvement is a property of the *situation*, not just the product: a $4 coffee is low involvement on a Tuesday and high involvement when you're buying it for a first date.
segments.tr: Note que o envolvimento é uma propriedade da *situação*, não apenas do produto: um café de $4 é de baixo envolvimento na terça-feira e de alto envolvimento quando você o compra para um primeiro encontro.

segments.src: Motivation — the tension that gets you moving.**
segments.tr: Motivação — a tensão que faz você se mover.**

segments.src: Motivation is an activated need: a gap between where you are and where you want to be, strong enough to push you toward action.
segments.tr: Motivação é uma necessidade ativada: uma lacuna entre onde você está e onde quer estar, forte o suficiente para empurrá-lo em direção à ação.

segments.src: Two flavors usually run at once:
segments.tr: Dois sabores geralmente correm de uma vez:

segments.src: - *Utilitarian* motives — solve the problem. Keep my feet from hurting. Get the laundry clean.
segments.tr: - Motivos *utilitários* — resolvem o problema. Evitam que meus pés doa. Deixam a roupa limpa.

segments.src: - *Hedonic* motives — feel something. Look like the kind of person who runs. Enjoy the unboxing.
segments.tr: - Motivos *hedônicos* — sentem algo. Parecem o tipo de pessoa que corre. Desfrutam do unboxing.

segments.src: Buyers rarely admit the second one out loud, which is exactly why survey answers and actual receipts often disagree.
segments.tr: Os compradores raramente admiten o segundo em voz alta, o que é exatamente o motivo pelo qual as respostas das pesquisas e os recibos reais muitas vezes discordam.

segments.src: Motives also conflict: wanting the upgrade *and* not wanting the bill (approach–avoidance) is why "0% APR for 12 months" closes so many sales — it doesn't change the price, it defuses the avoidance side.
segments.tr: Os motivos também entram em conflito: querer a atualização *e* não querer a conta (aproximação-evivação) é o motivo pelo qual "0% APR por 12 meses" fecha tantas vendas — não muda o preço, desativa o lado da evitação.

segments.src: Attitude — the stored verdict you carry around.**
segments.tr: Atitude — o veredito armazenado que você carrega.**

segments.src: An attitude is a learned, reasonably stable tendency to respond favorably or unfavorably to something.
segments.tr: Uma atitude é uma tendência aprendida, razoavelmente estável, de responder favoravelmente ou desfavoravelmente a algo.

segments.src: The classic model has three parts, often called ABC:
segments.tr: O modelo clássico tem três partes, frequentemente chamado de ABC:

segments.src: - **Affect** — how you feel about it ("Patagonia feels honest")
segments.tr: - **Afeto** — como você se sente sobre isso ("A Patagonia parece honesta")

segments.src: - **Behavior** — what you intend to do ("I'd buy it next time")
segments.tr: - **Comportamento** — o que você pretende fazer ("Eu compraria da próxima vez")

segments.src: - **Cognition** — what you believe about it ("their gear lasts a decade")
segments.tr: - **Cognição** — o que você acredita sobre isso ("o equipamento deles dura uma década")

segments.src: A useful working model is the multiattribute view: your overall attitude is roughly the sum of what you believe about each attribute, weighted by how much that attribute matters to you.
segments.tr: Um modelo de trabalho útil é a visão multiatributo: sua atitude geral é aproximadamente a soma do que você acredita sobre cada atributo, ponderada pelo quanto esse atributo importa para você.

segments.src: Attitude ≈ sum of (belief about attribute) × (importance of that attribute)
segments.tr: Attitude ≈ sum of (belief about attribute) × (importance of that attribute)

segments.src: That equation quietly explains most marketing tactics.
segments.tr: Essa equação explica silenciosamente a maioria das táticas de marketing.

segments.src: If people rate you low on an attribute, you can change the belief ("actually, we're 30% lighter").
segments.tr: Se as pessoas te avaliam mal em um atributo, você pode mudar a crença ("na verdade, somos 30% mais leves").

segments.src: Or change the weight ("weight isn't what causes injuries — cushioning is").
segments.tr: Ou mudar o peso ("o peso não é o que causa lesões — o amortecimento é").

segments.src: Or add a brand-new attribute nobody was scoring yet ("carbon plate").
segments.tr: Ou adicionar um atributo novíssimo que ninguém estava pontuando ainda ("placa de carbono").

segments.src: Changing what people care about is often cheaper than changing what they believe.
segments.tr: Mudar com o que as pessoas se importam costuma ser mais barato do que mudar no que elas acreditam.

segments.src: Reference groups — the invisible audience.**
segments.tr: Grupos de referência — o público invisível.**

segments.src: A reference group is any set of people you use as a benchmark for your own beliefs and behavior.
segments.tr: Um grupo de referência é qualquer conjunto de pessoas que você usa como referência para suas próprias crenças e comportamento.

segments.src: Three types matter: **membership** groups you actually belong to, **aspirational** groups you'd like to join, and **dissociative** groups you actively want to avoid resembling.
segments.tr: Três tipos importam: grupos de **associação** aos quais você realmente pertence, grupos **aspiracionais** aos quais gostaria de se juntar e grupos **dissociativos** que você quer evitar ativamente parecer.

segments.src: They influence you two ways: **normative** ("buy this or you won't fit in") and **informational** ("these people know things I don't, so I'll copy them").
segments.tr: Eles influenciam você de duas maneiras: **normativa** ("compre isso ou você não vai se encaixar") e **informacional** ("essas pessoas sabem coisas que eu não sei, então vou copiá-las").

segments.src: The practical rule researchers have found repeatedly: reference groups exert the most pull on things that are **publicly visible and non-essential** — the car in the driveway, the water bottle on your desk.
segments.tr: A regra prática que os pesquisadores encontraram repetidamente: os grupos de referência exercem mais força sobre coisas que são **publicamente visíveis e não essenciais** — o carro na garagem, a garrafa de água na sua mesa.

segments.src: They exert the least pull on private necessities.
segments.tr: Eles exercem menos força sobre necessidades privadas.

segments.src: Nobody chooses a mattress to impress the neighbors.
segments.tr: Ninguém escolhe um colchão para impressionar os vizinhos.

segments.src: ## In Everyday Life
segments.tr: ## Na Vida Quotidiana

segments.src: Say you live in Columbus and you just signed up for your first half marathon in October.
segments.tr: Digamos que você more em Columbus e acabou de se inscrever para sua primeira meia maratona em outubro.

segments.src: Here's all four forces in one shopping trip.
segments.tr: Aqui estão todas as quatro forças em uma única viagem de compras.

segments.src: **Motivation** shows up as two needs at once.
segments.tr: **Motivação** aparece como duas necessidades ao mesmo tempo.

segments.src: Utilitarian: your knees ache after three miles in old sneakers.
segments.tr: Utilitária: seus joelhos doem após três milhas em tênis velhos.

segments.src: Hedonic: you want to *be a runner*, not someone who owns running shoes.
segments.tr: Hedônica: você quer *ser um corredor*, não alguém que possui tênis de corrida.

segments.src: Both are real; only the first one comes out of your mouth at the store.
segments.tr: Ambas são reais; apenas a primeira sai da sua boca na loja.

segments.src: **Involvement** spikes.
segments.tr: **Envolvimento** dispara.

segments.src: This is a $165 purchase you'll wear for 400 miles, and picking wrong means shin splints in September.
segments.tr: Esta é uma compra de $165 que você vai usar por 400 milhas, e escolher errado significa dores nas canelas em setembro.

segments.src: So you do things you'd never do for socks: you read 40 minutes of reviews, watch two YouTube comparisons, and drive to a specialty shop to get your gait analyzed.
segments.tr: Então você faz coisas que nunca faria por meias: você lê 40 minutos de avaliações, assiste a duas comparações no YouTube e dirige até uma loja especializada para ter sua passada analisada.

segments.src: That's extended problem solving.
segments.tr: Isso é resolução de problemas estendida.

segments.src: Meanwhile you grab a $2 Gatorade at the register without a single conscious thought — same shopper, low involvement, pure habit.
segments.tr: Enquanto isso, você pega um Gatorade de $2 no caixa sem um único pensamento consciente — mesmo comprador, baixo envolvimento, puro hábito.

segments.src: **Attitude** is what you walk in with.
segments.tr: **Atitude** é com o que você entra.

segments.src: You already believe Brooks is "reliable but boring," Hoka is "cushioned but ugly," On is "trendy but pricey."
segments.tr: Você já acredita que a Brooks é "confiável mas chata", a Hoka é "amortecida mas feia", a On é "na moda mas cara".

segments.src: Those beliefs came from ads, a coworker, and a podcast — not from ever wearing the shoes.
segments.tr: Essas crenças vieram de anúncios, de um colega de trabalho e de um podcast — não de já ter usado os tênis.

segments.src: Now watch the salesperson work the equation: "Everyone worries about weight, but for a first half, cushioning is what saves your knees."
segments.tr: Agora observe o vendedor trabalhar a equação: "Todo mundo se preocupa com o peso, mas para uma primeira meia, o amortecimento é o que salva seus joelhos."

segments.src: He didn't argue with your beliefs.
segments.tr: Ele não discutiu com suas crenças.

segments.src: He reweighted the attributes, and suddenly the Hokas look smart.
segments.tr: Ele reponderou os atributos e de repente os Hokas parecem inteligentes.

segments.src: **Reference groups** close the deal.
segments.tr: **Grupos de referência** fecham o negócio.

segments.src: The Saturday morning run club you just joined is a membership group — you notice half of them wear the same shoe and you feel the pull to match (normative), and you also assume they know things you don't (informational).
segments.tr: O clube de corrida de sábado de manhã do qual você acabou de participar é um grupo de associação — você percebe que metade deles usa o mesmo tênis e sente a atração de combinar (normativa), e também assume que eles sabem coisas que você não sabe (informacional).

segments.src: The guy who ran Boston is your aspirational group; the Strava thread is a running commentary of both.
segments.tr: O cara que correu Boston é seu grupo aspiracional; o tópico do Strava é um comentário contínuo de ambos.

segments.src: And the shoes are highly visible and entirely optional — the exact conditions where reference group influence is strongest.
segments.tr: E os tênis são altamente visíveis e inteiramente opcionais — as condições exatas em que a influência do grupo de referência é mais forte.

segments.src: Your mattress, bought last spring, got none of this energy at all.
segments.tr: Seu colchão, comprado na primavera passada, não recebeu nada dessa energia.

segments.src: ## Three-Line Recap
segments.tr: ## Recapitulação de Três Linhas

segments.src: 1. **Involvement** decides how much thinking a purchase gets — driven by perceived risk (money, visibility, permanence), and it's situational, not just product-based.
segments.tr: 1. **Envolvimento** decide quanta reflexão uma compra recebe — impulsionada pelo risco percebido (dinheiro, visibilidade, permanência), e é situacional, não apenas baseada no produto.

segments.src: 2. **Motivation** is the activated need pushing you forward, and it's usually utilitarian and hedonic at once; **attitude** is your stored verdict, roughly beliefs weighted by importance — which is why reweighting attributes is a marketer's cheapest lever.
segments.tr: 2. **Motivação** é a necessidade ativada que te empurra para a frente, e geralmente é utilitária e hedônica ao mesmo tempo; **atitude** é seu veredito armazenado, aproximadamente crenças ponderadas pela importância — o que é a alavanca mais barata de um profissional de marketing.

segments.src: 3. **Reference groups** shape choices most powerfully when the product is publicly visible and non-essential, through normative (fit in) and informational (they know better) influence.
segments.tr: 3. **Grupos de referência** moldam escolhas com mais poder quando o produto é visível publicamente e não essencial, através de influência normativa (encaixar-se) e informacional (eles sabem melhor).

segments.tr: ## ✅ Autoteste

segments.tr: **P1.** Qual compra tem mais probabilidade de ser de *alto envolvimento* para um comprador típico?

segments.tr: A.

segments.tr: Um anel de noivado de $2.400

segments.tr: Reabastecer a mesma marca de detergente para louça

segments.tr: **P2.** Verdadeiro ou Falso: Uma marca pode melhorar sua atitude geral em relação a ela *sem* mudar nenhuma de suas crenças existentes sobre seus recursos.

segments.tr: **P3.** A influência do grupo de referência tende a ser **mais forte** para que tipo de produto?

segments.tr: Necessidades privadas (pasta de dente guardada em um armário)

segments.src: ## 📚 Today's Terms
segments.tr: ## 📚 Termos de Hoje

segments.src: - **Involvement** — The personal relevance and perceived risk of a purchase, which determines how much effort the decision gets.
segments.tr: - **Envolvimento** — A relevância pessoal e o risco percebido de uma compra, o que determina quanto esforço a decisão recebe.

segments.src: - **Motivation** — An activated need creating enough tension to drive goal-directed behavior; typically utilitarian (solve a problem) and/or hedonic (feel something).
segments.tr: - **Motivação** — Uma necessidade ativada que cria tensão suficiente para impulsionar o comportamento direcionado a objetivos; tipicamente utilitária (resolver um problema) e/ou hedônica (sentir algo).

segments.src: - **Attitude** — A learned, relatively stable favorable or unfavorable predisposition toward an object, made up of affect, behavior, and cognition.
segments.tr: - **Atitude** — Uma predisposição aprendida, relativamente estável, favorável ou desfavorável em relação a um objeto, composta de afeto, comportamento e cognição.

segments.src: - **Multiattribute model** — The view that overall attitude equals the sum of beliefs about each attribute weighted by that attribute's importance.
segments.tr: - **Modelo multiatributo** — A visão de que a atitude geral é igual à soma das crenças sobre cada atributo ponderadas pela importância desse atributo.

segments.src: - **Reference group** — People used as a benchmark for one's own beliefs and behavior; membership, aspirational, or dissociative, acting through normative or informational influence.
segments.tr: - **Grupo de referência** — Pessoas usadas como referência para as crenças e o comportamento de alguém; de associação, aspiracional ou dissociativo, agindo através de influência normativa ou informacional.

segments.src: *Answers: **Q1 — B.** Involvement rises with money at stake, social visibility, permanence, and the cost of being wrong; a ring maxes out all four, while milk, dish soap, and gum are habitual, low-risk buys.
segments.tr: *Respostas: **P1 — B.** O envolvimento aumenta com o dinheiro em jogo, a visibilidade social, a permanência e o custo de estar errado; um anel maximiza todos os quatro, enquanto o leite, o detergente e o chiclete são compras habituais e de baixo risco.

segments.src: **Q2 — True.** Under the multiattribute model, a brand can raise its score by changing the *importance weights* ("cushioning matters more than weight") or by introducing an attribute you weren't scoring at all — no belief revision required.
segments.tr: **P2 — Verdadeiro.** Sob o modelo multiatributo, uma marca pode aumentar sua pontuação mudando os *pesos de importância* ("o amortecimento importa mais do que o peso") ou introduzindo um atributo que você não estava pontuando — nenhuma revisão de crença necessária.

segments.src: **Q3 — B.** Influence is greatest when a product is both seen by others (so norms apply) and optional (so the choice signals something about you); private necessities like toothpaste are the weakest case.*
segments.tr: **P3 — B.** A influência é maior quando um produto é visto pelos outros (então as normas se aplicam) e é opcional (então a escolha sinaliza algo sobre você); necessidades privadas como pasta de dente são o caso mais fraco.*

segments.tr: - **Kognisi** — apa yang Anda yakini tentang hal itu ("peralatan mereka bertahan satu dekade")

segments.src: A useful working model is the multiattribute view: your overall attitude is roughly the sum of what you believe about each attribute, weighted by how much that attribute matters to you.
segments.tr: Model kerja yang berguna adalah pandangan multiatribut: sikap keseluruhan Anda kira-kira merupakan jumlah dari apa yang Anda yakini tentang setiap atribut, ditimbang oleh seberapa besar atribut itu penting bagi Anda.

segments.src: Attitude ≈ sum of (belief about attribute) × (importance of that attribute)
segments.tr: Attitude ≈ sum of (belief about attribute) × (importance of that attribute)

segments.src: That equation quietly explains most marketing tactics.
segments.tr: Persamaan itu secara diam-diam menjelaskan sebagian besar taktik pemasaran.

segments.src: If people rate you low on an attribute, you can change the belief ("actually, we're 30% lighter").
segments.tr: Jika orang menilai Anda rendah pada suatu atribut, Anda dapat mengubah keyakinan ("sebenarnya, kami 30% lebih ringan").

segments.src: Or change the weight ("weight isn't what causes injuries — cushioning is").
segments.tr: Atau mengubah bobot ("berat bukanlah penyebab cedera — bantalanlah yang menyebabkannya").

segments.src: Or add a brand-new attribute nobody was scoring yet ("carbon plate").
segments.tr: Atau menambahkan atribut baru yang belum dinilai oleh siapa pun ("pelat karbon").

segments.src: Changing what people care about is often cheaper than changing what they believe.
segments.tr: Mengubah apa yang dipedulikan orang seringkali lebih murah daripada mengubah apa yang mereka yakini.

segments.src: Reference groups — the invisible audience.**
segments.tr: Kelompok acuan — audiens tak terlihat.**

segments.src: A reference group is any set of people you use as a benchmark for your own beliefs and behavior.
segments.tr: Kelompok acuan adalah kelompok orang mana pun yang Anda gunakan sebagai tolok ukur untuk keyakinan dan perilaku Anda sendiri.

segments.src: Three types matter: **membership** groups you actually belong to, **aspirational** groups you'd like to join, and **dissociative** groups you actively want to avoid resembling.
segments.tr: Tiga jenis yang penting: kelompok **keanggotaan** yang benar-benar Anda miliki, kelompok **aspirasional** yang ingin Anda gabungi, dan kelompok **disosiatif** yang secara aktif ingin Anda hindari kemiripannya.

segments.src: They influence you two ways: **normative** ("buy this or you won't fit in") and **informational** ("these people know things I don't, so I'll copy them").
segments.tr: Mereka memengaruhi Anda dengan dua cara: **normatif** ("beli ini atau Anda tidak akan cocok") dan **informasional** ("orang-orang ini tahu hal-hal yang tidak saya ketahui, jadi saya akan meniru mereka").

segments.src: The practical rule researchers have found repeatedly: reference groups exert the most pull on things that are **publicly visible and non-essential** — the car in the driveway, the water bottle on your desk.
segments.tr: Aturan praktis yang ditemukan para peneliti secara berulang-ulang: kelompok acuan memberikan pengaruh terbesar pada hal-hal yang **terlihat secara publik dan tidak esensial** — mobil di jalan masuk, botol air di meja Anda.

segments.src: They exert the least pull on private necessities.
segments.tr: Mereka memberikan pengaruh paling sedikit pada kebutuhan pribadi.

segments.src: Nobody chooses a mattress to impress the neighbors.
segments.tr: Tidak ada yang memilih kasur untuk mengesankan tetangga.

segments.src: ## In Everyday Life
segments.tr: ## Dalam Kehidupan Sehari-hari

segments.src: Say you live in Columbus and you just signed up for your first half marathon in October.
segments.tr: Katakanlah Anda tinggal di Columbus dan Anda baru saja mendaftar untuk setengah maraton pertama Anda di bulan Oktober.

segments.src: Here's all four forces in one shopping trip.
segments.tr: Berikut adalah keempat kekuatan dalam satu perjalanan belanja.

segments.src: **Motivation** shows up as two needs at once.
segments.tr: **Motivasi** muncul sebagai dua kebutuhan sekaligus.

segments.src: Utilitarian: your knees ache after three miles in old sneakers.
segments.tr: Utilitarian: lutut Anda sakit setelah tiga mil dengan sepatu kets lama.

segments.src: Hedonic: you want to *be a runner*, not someone who owns running shoes.
segments.tr: Hedonis: Anda ingin *menjadi seorang pelari*, bukan seseorang yang memiliki sepatu lari.

segments.src: Both are real; only the first one comes out of your mouth at the store.
segments.tr: Keduanya nyata; hanya yang pertama yang keluar dari mulut Anda di toko.

segments.src: **Involvement** spikes.
segments.tr: **Keterlibatan** melonjak.

segments.src: This is a $165 purchase you'll wear for 400 miles, and picking wrong means shin splints in September.
segments.tr: Ini adalah pembelian senilai $165 yang akan Anda pakai selama 400 mil, dan salah pilih berarti belat tulang kering di bulan September.

segments.src: So you do things you'd never do for socks: you read 40 minutes of reviews, watch two YouTube comparisons, and drive to a specialty shop to get your gait analyzed.
segments.tr: Jadi Anda melakukan hal-hal yang tidak akan pernah Anda lakukan untuk kaus kaki: Anda membaca ulasan selama 40 menit, menonton dua perbandingan YouTube, dan berkendara ke toko khusus untuk menganalisis cara berjalan Anda.

segments.src: That's extended problem solving.
segments.tr: Itulah pemecahan masalah yang diperluas.

segments.src: Meanwhile you grab a $2 Gatorade at the register without a single conscious thought — same shopper, low involvement, pure habit.
segments.tr: Sementara itu, Anda mengambil Gatorade seharga $2 di kasir tanpa satu pikiran sadar pun — pembeli yang sama, keterlibatan rendah, kebiasaan murni.

segments.src: **Attitude** is what you walk in with.
segments.tr: **Sikap** adalah apa yang Anda bawa masuk.

segments.src: You already believe Brooks is "reliable but boring," Hoka is "cushioned but ugly," On is "trendy but pricey."
segments.tr: Anda sudah percaya bahwa Brooks itu "andal tetapi membosankan," Hoka itu "empuk tetapi jelek," On itu "tren tetapi mahal."

segments.src: Those beliefs came from ads, a coworker, and a podcast — not from ever wearing the shoes.
segments.tr: Keyakinan tersebut berasal dari iklan, seorang rekan kerja, dan sebuah siniar — bukan dari pernah mengenakan sepatu tersebut.

segments.src: Now watch the salesperson work the equation: "Everyone worries about weight, but for a first half, cushioning is what saves your knees."
segments.tr: Sekarang perhatikan tenaga penjual mengerjakan persamaan tersebut: "Semua orang khawatir tentang berat badan, tetapi untuk setengah pertama, bantalan adalah yang menyelamatkan lutut Anda."

segments.src: He didn't argue with your beliefs.
segments.tr: Dia tidak berdebat dengan keyakinan Anda.

segments.src: He reweighted the attributes, and suddenly the Hokas look smart.
segments.tr: Dia menimbang ulang atribut-atribut tersebut, dan tiba-tiba Hoka terlihat cerdas.

segments.src: **Reference groups** close the deal.
segments.tr: **Kelompok acuan** menutup kesepakatan.

segments.src: The Saturday morning run club you just joined is a membership group — you notice half of them wear the same shoe and you feel the pull to match (normative), and you also assume they know things you don't (informational).
segments.tr: Klub lari Sabtu pagi yang baru saja Anda ikuti adalah kelompok keanggotaan — Anda melihat separuh dari mereka mengenakan sepatu yang sama dan Anda merasakan dorongan untuk mencocokkan (normatif), dan Anda juga berasumsi bahwa mereka mengetahui hal-hal yang tidak Anda ketahui (informasional).

segments.src: The guy who ran Boston is your aspirational group; the Strava thread is a running commentary of both.
segments.tr: Pria yang berlari di Boston adalah kelompok aspirasional Anda; utas Strava adalah komentar yang berjalan dari keduanya.

segments.src: And the shoes are highly visible and entirely optional — the exact conditions where reference group influence is strongest.
segments.tr: Dan sepatu tersebut sangat terlihat dan sepenuhnya opsional — kondisi persis di mana pengaruh kelompok acuan paling kuat.

segments.src: Your mattress, bought last spring, got none of this energy at all.
segments.tr: Kasur Anda, yang dibeli musim semi lalu, sama sekali tidak mendapatkan energi ini.

segments.src: ## Three-Line Recap
segments.tr: ## Rekap Tiga Baris

segments.src: 1. **Involvement** decides how much thinking a purchase gets — driven by perceived risk (money, visibility, permanence), and it's situational, not just product-based.
segments.tr: 1. **Keterlibatan** memutuskan seberapa banyak pemikiran yang didapat dari sebuah pembelian — didorong oleh risiko yang dirasakan (uang, visibilitas, kepermanenan), dan ini situasional, bukan hanya berbasis produk.

segments.src: 2. **Motivation** is the activated need pushing you forward, and it's usually utilitarian and hedonic at once; **attitude** is your stored verdict, roughly beliefs weighted by importance — which is why reweighting attributes is a marketer's cheapest lever.
segments.tr: 2. **Motivasi** adalah kebutuhan teraktivasi yang mendorong Anda maju, dan biasanya bersifat utilitarian dan hedonis sekaligus; **sikap** adalah putusan tersimpan Anda, secara kasar keyakinan yang ditimbang berdasarkan kepentingan — itulah mengapa menimbang ulang atribut adalah tuas termurah bagi pemasar.

segments.src: 3. **Reference groups** shape choices most powerfully when the product is publicly visible and non-essential, through normative (fit in) and informational (they know better) influence.
segments.tr: 3. **Kelompok acuan** membentuk pilihan paling kuat ketika produk tersebut terlihat secara publik dan tidak esensial, melalui pengaruh normatif (cocok) dan informasional (mereka lebih tahu).

segments.src: ## 📚 Today's Terms
segments.tr: ## 📚 Istilah Hari Ini

segments.src: - **Involvement** — The personal relevance and perceived risk of a purchase, which determines how much effort the decision gets.
segments.tr: - **Keterlibatan** — Relevansi pribadi dan risiko yang dirasakan dari sebuah pembelian, yang menentukan seberapa besar upaya keputusan tersebut.

segments.src: - **Motivation** — An activated need creating enough tension to drive goal-directed behavior; typically utilitarian (solve a problem) and/or hedonic (feel something).
segments.tr: - **Motivasi** — Kebutuhan teraktivasi yang menciptakan ketegangan yang cukup untuk mendorong perilaku yang diarahkan pada tujuan; biasanya utilitarian (memecahkan masalah) dan/atau hedonis (merasakan sesuatu).

segments.src: - **Attitude** — A learned, relatively stable favorable or unfavorable predisposition toward an object, made up of affect, behavior, and cognition.
segments.tr: - **Sikap** — Kecenderungan yang dipelajari, relatif stabil, baik atau tidak baik terhadap suatu objek, yang terdiri dari afek, perilaku, dan kognisi.

segments.src: - **Multiattribute model** — The view that overall attitude equals the sum of beliefs about each attribute weighted by that attribute's importance.
segments.tr: - **Model multiatribut** — Pandangan bahwa sikap keseluruhan sama dengan jumlah keyakinan tentang setiap atribut yang ditimbang oleh kepentingan atribut tersebut.

segments.src: - **Reference group** — People used as a benchmark for one's own beliefs and behavior; membership, aspirational, or dissociative, acting through normative or informational influence.
segments.tr: - **Kelompok acuan** — Orang yang digunakan sebagai tolok ukur untuk keyakinan dan perilaku seseorang; keanggotaan, aspirasional, atau disosiatif, bertindak melalui pengaruh normatif atau informasional.

segments.src: *Answers: **Q1 — B.** Involvement rises with money at stake, social visibility, permanence, and the cost of being wrong; a ring maxes out all four, while milk, dish soap, and gum are habitual, low-risk buys.
segments.tr: *Jawaban: **Q1 — B.** Keterlibatan meningkat dengan uang yang dipertaruhkan, visibilitas sosial, kepermanenan, dan biaya salah; sebuah cincin memaksimalkan keempatnya, sementara susu, sabun cuci piring, dan permen karet adalah pembelian kebiasaan berisiko rendah.

segments.src: **Q2 — True.** Under the multiattribute model, a brand can raise its score by changing the *importance weights* ("cushioning matters more than weight") or by introducing an attribute you weren't scoring at all — no belief revision required.
segments.tr: **Q2 — Benar.** Di bawah model multiatribut, sebuah merek dapat menaikkan skornya dengan mengubah *bobot kepentingan* ("bantalan lebih penting daripada berat") atau dengan memperkenalkan atribut yang tidak Anda nilai sama sekali — tidak diperlukan revisi keyakinan.

segments.src: **Q3 — B.** Influence is greatest when a product is both seen by others (so norms apply) and optional (so the choice signals something about you); private necessities like toothpaste are the weakest case.*
segments.tr: **Q3 — B.** Pengaruh paling besar ketika suatu produk dilihat oleh orang lain (sehingga norma berlaku) dan opsional (sehingga pilihan tersebut menandakan sesuatu tentang Anda); kebutuhan pribadi seperti pasta gigi adalah kasus yang paling lemah.*

ja.title: [Marketing 101 #4] ランニングシューズには3週間悩み、ガムには3秒しか悩まない理由

segments.src: > Four forces decide what you buy — how much you care (involvement), what need is driving you (motivation), what you already believe (attitude), and who you're secretly buying for (reference groups).
segments.tr: > あなたが何を買うかを決定するのは4つの力です — どれほど重要視しているか（関与度）、どのような欲求が駆り立てているか（動機）、すでに信じていること（態度）、そして秘密裏に誰のために買っているのか（準拠集団）。

segments.src: ## Today's Concept
segments.tr: ## 今日のコンセプト

segments.src: Most of us think we shop rationally: compare options, pick the best one, done.
segments.tr: 私たちのほとんどは、合理的にお買い物をしていると考えています。選択肢を比較し、ベストなものを選び、終わり、という具合です。

segments.src: In reality, the amount of thinking you do varies wildly from purchase to purchase — and it's fairly predictable.
segments.tr: しかし現実には、行う思考の量は購入ごとに大きく異なり、それはかなり予測可能です。

segments.src: Consumer behavior researchers explain that variation with four building blocks.
segments.tr: 消費者行動の研究者たちは、その変動を4つの構成要素で説明しています。

segments.src: Involvement — how much this purchase matters to you.**
segments.tr: 関与度 — この購入があなたにとってどれほど重要か。**

segments.src: Involvement is the personal relevance of a purchase, and it rises with the perceived risk: money at stake, how visible the choice is to other people, how long you're stuck with it, and how bad it feels to get it wrong.
segments.tr: 関与度とは、購入における個人的な関連性であり、知覚されるリスク（リスクとなるお金、その選択が他の人からどれだけ見えるか、どれくらい長く付き合うことになるか、間違えたときにどれほど嫌な気持ちになるか）とともに上昇します。

segments.src: High involvement means an extended decision process — research, spreadsheets, reviews, second opinions.
segments.tr: 高関与とは、拡張された決定プロセス（リサーチ、スプレッドシート、レビュー、セカンドオピニオン）を意味します。

segments.src: Low involvement means habit or impulse: you grab the familiar package and move on.
segments.tr: 低関与とは、習慣や衝動を意味します。おなじみのパッケージを掴んで次に進みます。

segments.src: Same shopper, same day, completely different behavior.
segments.tr: 同じ買い物客、同じ日でありながら、まったく異なる行動です。

segments.src: Note that involvement is a property of the *situation*, not just the product: a $4 coffee is low involvement on a Tuesday and high involvement when you're buying it for a first date.
segments.tr: なお、関与度は製品だけでなく、*状況*の特性でもあります。4ドルのコーヒーは火曜日には低関与ですが、初めてのデートのために買うときは高関与になります。

segments.src: Motivation — the tension that gets you moving.**
segments.tr: 動機 — あなたを動かす緊張感。**

segments.src: Motivation is an activated need: a gap between where you are and where you want to be, strong enough to push you toward action.
segments.tr: 動機とは活性化された欲求であり、現在地と行きたい場所のギャップであり、行動へとあなたを突き動かすのに十分な強さを持つものです。

segments.src: Two flavors usually run at once:
segments.tr: 通常、2つの側面が同時に働きます。

segments.src: - *Utilitarian* motives — solve the problem. Keep my feet from hurting. Get the laundry clean.
segments.tr: - *実用的な（Utilitarian）*動機 — 問題を解決する。足が痛むのを防ぐ。洗濯物をきれいに仕上げる。

segments.src: - *Hedonic* motives — feel something. Look like the kind of person who runs. Enjoy the unboxing.
segments.tr: - *快楽的な（Hedonic）*動機 — 何かを感じる。走るような人のように見える。開封を楽しむ。

segments.src: Buyers rarely admit the second one out loud, which is exactly why survey answers and actual receipts often disagree.
segments.tr: 買い手は2つ目を声に出して認めることはめったにありません。それがまさに、アンケートの回答と実際のレシートがしばしば食い違う理由です。

segments.src: Motives also conflict: wanting the upgrade *and* not wanting the bill (approach–avoidance) is why "0% APR for 12 months" closes so many sales — it doesn't change the price, it defuses the avoidance side.
segments.tr: 動機は衝突することもあります。アップグレードを望む気持ち*と*請求書を望まない気持ち（接近・回避）のせいで、「12ヶ月間0% APR」があんなにも多くのセールを成立させるのです。それは価格を変えるのではなく、回避の側面を和らげるのです。

segments.src: Attitude — the stored verdict you carry around.**
segments.tr: 態度 — あなたが持ち歩いている蓄積された判定。**

segments.src: An attitude is a learned, reasonably stable tendency to respond favorably or unfavorably to something.
segments.tr: 態度とは、何らかのものに対して好意的または非好意的に反応する、学習された、比較的安定した傾向です。

segments.src: The classic model has three parts, often called ABC:
segments.tr: 古典的なモデルには3つの部分があり、通常ABCと呼ばれます。

segments.src: - **Affect** — how you feel about it ("Patagonia feels honest")
segments.tr: - **感情（Affect）** — それに対する感じ方（「パタゴニアは誠実に感じる」）

segments.src: - **Behavior** — what you intend to do ("I'd buy it next time")
segments.tr: - **行動（Behavior）** — 何をしようとする意図（「今度買おう」）

segments.src: - **Cognition** — what you believe about it ("their gear lasts a decade")
segments.tr: - **認知（Cognition）** — それについて信じていること（「彼らのギアは10年持つ」）

segments.src: A useful working model is the multiattribute view: your overall attitude is roughly the sum of what you believe about each attribute, weighted by how much that attribute matters to you.
segments.tr: 役立つ実用的なモデルは、マルチ属性ビューです。あなたの全体的な態度は、各属性について信じていることの総和に、その属性があなたにとってどれほど重要であるかによる重み付けをしたものにおおよそ等しくなります。

segments.src: Attitude ≈ sum of (belief about attribute) × (importance of that attribute)
segments.tr: Attitude ≈ sum of (belief about attribute) × (importance of that attribute)

segments.src: That equation quietly explains most marketing tactics.
segments.tr: その方程式は、ほとんどのマーケティング戦術を静かに説明しています。

segments.src: If people rate you low on an attribute, you can change the belief ("actually, we're 30% lighter").
segments.tr: 人々があなたをある属性で低く評価する場合、その信念を変えることができます（「実際には30%軽量です」）。

segments.src: Or change the weight ("weight isn't what causes injuries — cushioning is").
segments.tr: あるいは重み付けを変える（「体重が怪我を引き起こすのではなく、クッション性です」）。

segments.src: Or add a brand-new attribute nobody was scoring yet ("carbon plate").
segments.tr: あるいは、まだ誰もスコアをつけていなかったまったく新しい属性を追加する（「カーボンプレート」）。

segments.src: Changing what people care about is often cheaper than changing what they believe.
segments.tr: 人々が気にかけていることを変えることは、彼らが信じていることを変えることよりもしばしば安上がりです。

segments.src: Reference groups — the invisible audience.**
segments.tr: 準拠集団 — 目に見えない観客。**

segments.src: A reference group is any set of people you use as a benchmark for your own beliefs and behavior.
segments.tr: 準拠集団とは、自分自身の信念や行動のベンチマークとして使用するあらゆる人々のグループです。

segments.src: Three types matter: **membership** groups you actually belong to, **aspirational** groups you'd like to join, and **dissociative** groups you actively want to avoid resembling.
segments.tr: 3つのタイプが重要です。実際に所属している**メンバーシップ**グループ、参加したい**志望**グループ、似ていることを積極的に避けたい**解離**グループです。

segments.src: They influence you two ways: **normative** ("buy this or you won't fit in") and **informational** ("these people know things I don't, so I'll copy them").
segments.tr: それらは2つの方法であなたに影響を与えます。**規範的**（「これを買わないと馴染めない」）と**情報的**（「この人たちは自分知らないことを知っているから、真似しよう」）。

segments.src: The practical rule researchers have found repeatedly: reference groups exert the most pull on things that are **publicly visible and non-essential** — the car in the driveway, the water bottle on your desk.
segments.tr: 研究者たちが繰り返し発見してきた実用的なルールは、準拠集団が最も大きな影響を及ぼすのは、**公に見えて非本質的**なもの（駐車場の車、机の上のウォーターボトル）であるということです。

segments.src: They exert the least pull on private necessities.
segments.tr: プライベートな必需品に対しては、最も影響力が弱まります。

segments.src: Nobody chooses a mattress to impress the neighbors.
segments.tr: 隣人を感心させるためにマットレスを選ぶ人はいません。

segments.src: ## In Everyday Life
segments.tr: ## 日常生活において

segments.src: Say you live in Columbus and you just signed up for your first half marathon in October.
segments.tr: あなたがコロンバスに住んでいて、10月の初めてのハーフマラソンに申し込んだとしましょう。

segments.src: Here's all four forces in one shopping trip.
segments.tr: ここに、1回の買い物旅行に4つの力がすべて現れています。

segments.src: **Motivation** shows up as two needs at once.
segments.tr: **動機**は、一度に2つの欲求として現れます。

segments.src: Utilitarian: your knees ache after three miles in old sneakers.
segments.tr: 実用的：古いスニーカーで3マイル走ると膝が痛む。

segments.src: Hedonic: you want to *be a runner*, not someone who owns running shoes.
segments.tr: 快楽的：ランニングシューズを所有する人ではなく、*ランナーになりたい*。

segments.src: Both are real; only the first one comes out of your mouth at the store.
segments.tr: どちらも本物ですが、店で口から出るのは最初のものだけです。

segments.src: **Involvement** spikes.
segments.tr: **関与度**が急上昇します。

segments.src: This is a $165 purchase you'll wear for 400 miles, and picking wrong means shin splints in September.
segments.tr: これは400マイル着用する165ドルの買い物であり、間違った選択をすることは9月にシンスプリントになることを意味します。

segments.src: So you do things you'd never do for socks: you read 40 minutes of reviews, watch two YouTube comparisons, and drive to a specialty shop to get your gait analyzed.
segments.tr: そのため、靴下のために絶対にしないようなことをします。40分間のレビューを読み、2つのYouTubeの比較動画を見、専門ショップまで車を運転して歩行分析をしてもらうのです。

segments.src: That's extended problem solving.
segments.tr: それが拡張的問題解決です。

segments.src: Meanwhile you grab a $2 Gatorade at the register without a single conscious thought — same shopper, low involvement, pure habit.
segments.tr: 一方で、レジで意識的な思考を1つもすることなく2ドルのゲータレードを掴みます — 同じ買い物客、低関与、純粋な習慣です。

segments.src: **Attitude** is what you walk in with.
segments.tr: **態度**とは、あなたが足を踏み入れるときに持っているものです。

segments.src: You already believe Brooks is "reliable but boring," Hoka is "cushioned but ugly," On is "trendy but pricey."
segments.tr: あなたはすでに、ブルックスは「信頼できるが退屈」、ホカは「クッション性はあるがダサい」、オンは「トレンディだが高価」と信じています。

segments.src: Those beliefs came from ads, a coworker, and a podcast — not from ever wearing the shoes.
segments.tr: それらの信念は、実際に靴を履いたからではなく、広告、同僚、ポッドキャストから得たものです。

segments.src: Now watch the salesperson work the equation: "Everyone worries about weight, but for a first half, cushioning is what saves your knees."
segments.tr: 今度は販売員がその方程式をどう扱うかを見てみましょう。「誰もが重さを心配しますが、最初のハーフにとっては、膝を守るのはクッション性です。」

segments.src: He didn't argue with your beliefs.
segments.tr: 彼はあなたの信念に反論しませんでした。

segments.src: He reweighted the attributes, and suddenly the Hokas look smart.
segments.tr: 彼は属性の重み付けを直し、突然ホカが賢い選択に見えてきます。

segments.src: **Reference groups** close the deal.
segments.tr: **準拠集団**が取引を成立させます。

segments.src: The Saturday morning run club you just joined is a membership group — you notice half of them wear the same shoe and you feel the pull to match (normative), and you also assume they know things you don't (informational).
segments.tr: あなたが参加したばかりの土曜日の朝のランニングクラブはメンバーシップグループです。半分が同じ靴を履いていることに気づき、合わせなければというプレッシャー（規範的）を感じ、また彼らは自分が知らないことを知っていると仮定します（情報的）。

segments.src: The guy who ran Boston is your aspirational group; the Strava thread is a running commentary of both.
segments.tr: ボストンを走った男性はあなたの志望グループであり、Stravaのスレッドはその両方の継続的な解説です。

segments.src: And the shoes are highly visible and entirely optional — the exact conditions where reference group influence is strongest.
segments.tr: そして靴は非常に目立ち、完全に任意のものであるため、準拠集団の影響が最も強くなるまさにその条件が揃っています。

segments.src: Your mattress, bought last spring, got none of this energy at all.
segments.tr: 昨年の春に購入したマットレスには、このエネルギーはまったく注がれませんでした。

segments.src: ## Three-Line Recap
segments.tr: ## 3行のまとめ

segments.src: 1. **Involvement** decides how much thinking a purchase gets — driven by perceived risk (money, visibility, permanence), and it's situational, not just product-based.
segments.tr: 1. **関与度**は、購入にかかる思考の量を決定します — 知覚されるリスク（お金、可視性、永続性）によって駆動され、製品ベースだけでなく状況的なものです。

segments.src: 2. **Motivation** is the activated need pushing you forward, and it's usually utilitarian and hedonic at once; **attitude** is your stored verdict, roughly beliefs weighted by importance — which is why reweighting attributes is a marketer's cheapest lever.
segments.tr: 2. **Motivation** はあなたを前進させる活性化された欲求であり、通常は実用的かつ快楽的が同時に起こります。**態度**はあなたが蓄積した判定であり、重要度によって重み付けされた信念におおよそ等しいものです。これが、属性の重み付けを変えることがマーケターにとって最も安上がりなレバーである理由です。

segments.src: 3. **Reference groups** shape choices most powerfully when the product is publicly visible and non-essential, through normative (fit in) and informational (they know better) influence.
segments.tr: 3. **準拠集団**は、製品が公に見え、非本質的であるときに、規範的（馴染む）および情報的（彼らはよりよく知っている）影響を通じて、選択を最も強力に形作ります。

segments.tr: ## ✅ セルフクイズ

segments.src: ## 📚 Today's Terms
segments.tr: ## 📚 今日の用語

segments.src: - **Involvement** — The personal relevance and perceived risk of a purchase, which determines how much effort the decision gets.
segments.tr: - **関与度（Involvement）** — 購入の個人的な関連性と知覚されるリスクであり、決定にどれだけの労力が費やされるかを決定します。

segments.src: - **Motivation** — An activated need creating enough tension to drive goal-directed behavior; typically utilitarian (solve a problem) and/or hedonic (feel something).
segments.tr: - **動機（Motivation）** — 目標に向けた行動を駆動するのに十分な緊張感を生み出す活性化された欲求。通常、実用的（問題を解決する）および/または快楽的（何かを感じる）です。

segments.src: - **Attitude** — A learned, relatively stable favorable or unfavorable predisposition toward an object, made up of affect, behavior, and cognition.
segments.tr: - **態度（Attitude）** — 対象に対する、学習された、比較的安定した好意的または非好意的な傾向であり、感情、行動、認知で構成されています。

segments.src: - **Multiattribute model** — The view that overall attitude equals the sum of beliefs about each attribute weighted by that attribute's importance.
segments.tr: - **マルチ属性モデル（Multiattribute model）** — 全体的な態度が、各属性についての信念の総和に、その属性の重要度を掛け合わせたものに等しいという見方。

segments.src: - **Reference group** — People used as a benchmark for one's own beliefs and behavior; membership, aspirational, or dissociative, acting through normative or informational influence.
segments.tr: - **準拠集団（Reference group）** — 自身の信念や行動のベンチマークとして使用される人々。メンバーシップ、志望、または解離であり、規範的または情報的影響を通じて作用します。

segments.src: *Answers: **Q1 — B.** Involvement rises with money at stake, social visibility, permanence, and the cost of being wrong; a ring maxes out all four, while milk, dish soap, and gum are habitual, low-risk buys.
segments.tr: *回答: **Q1 — B.** 関与度は、リスクとなるお金、社会的可視性、永続性、および間違えたときのコストとともに上昇します。指輪は4つすべてを最大化しますが、ミルク、食器用洗剤、ガムは習慣的で低リスクの買い物です。

segments.src: **Q2 — True.** Under the multiattribute model, a brand can raise its score by changing the *importance weights* ("cushioning matters more than weight") or by introducing an attribute you weren't scoring at all — no belief revision required.
segments.tr: **Q2 — 正。** マルチ属性モデルの下では、ブランドは*重要度の重み付け*を変更する（「重さよりもクッション性が重要である」）か、スコアをつけていなかった属性を導入することによってスコアを上げることができます — 信念の改訂は必要ありません。

segments.src: **Q3 — B.** Influence is greatest when a product is both seen by others (so norms apply) and optional (so the choice signals something about you); private necessities like toothpaste are the weakest case.*
segments.tr: **Q3 — B.** 影響は、製品が他者に見られ（したがって規範が適用される）、かつ任意である（したがって選択があなたについて何かを示している）場合に最も大きくなります。歯磨き粉のようなプライベートな必需品は最も弱いケースです。*

de.title: [Marketing 101 #4] Warum Sie drei Wochen lang über Laufschuhen und drei Sekunden lang über Kaugummis grübeln

segments.src: > Four forces decide what you buy — how much you care (involvement), what need is driving you (motivation), what you already believe (attitude), and who you're secretly buying for (reference groups).
segments.tr: > Vier Kräfte bestimmen, was Sie kaufen — wie sehr es Sie kümmert (Involvement), welche Bedürfnisse Sie antreiben (Motivation), was Sie bereits glauben (Einstellung) und für wen Sie heimlich kaufen (Bezugsgruppen).

segments.src: ## Today's Concept
segments.tr: ## Das heutige Konzept

segments.src: Most of us think we shop rationally: compare options, pick the best one, done.
segments.tr: Die meisten von uns denken, sie kaufen rational: Optionen vergleichen, die beste auswählen, fertig.

segments.src: In reality, the amount of thinking you do varies wildly from purchase to purchase — and it's fairly predictable.
segments.tr: In Wirklichkeit variiert der Grad an Nachdenken von Kauf zu Kauf stark — und das ist ziemlich vorhersehbar.

segments.src: Consumer behavior researchers explain that variation with four building blocks.
segments.tr: Verbraucherverhaltensforscher erklären diese Variation mit vier Bausteinen.

segments.src: Involvement — how much this purchase matters to you.**
segments.tr: Involvement — wie wichtig Ihnen dieser Kauf ist.**

segments.src: Involvement is the personal relevance of a purchase, and it rises with the perceived risk: money at stake, how visible the choice is to other people, how long you're stuck with it, and how bad it feels to get it wrong.
segments.tr: Involvement ist die persönliche Relevanz eines Kaufs und steigt mit dem wahrgenommenen Risiko: Geld auf dem Spiel, wie sichtbar die Wahl für andere Menschen ist, wie lange Sie daran gebunden sind und wie schlecht es sich anfühlt, falsch zu liegen.

segments.src: High involvement means an extended decision process — research, spreadsheets, reviews, second opinions.
segments.tr: Hohes Involvement bedeutet einen erweiterten Entscheidungsprozess — Recherche, Tabellen, Bewertungen, Zweitmeinungen.

segments.src: Low involvement means habit or impulse: you grab the familiar package and move on.
segments.tr: Geringes Involvement bedeutet Gewohnheit oder Impuls: Sie greifen zur vertrauten Verpackung und gehen weiter.

segments.src: Same shopper, same day, completely different behavior.
segments.tr: Gleicher Käufer, gleicher Tag, völlig anderes Verhalten.

segments.src: Note that involvement is a property of the *situation*, not just the product: a $4 coffee is low involvement on a Tuesday and high involvement when you're buying it for a first date.
segments.tr: Beachten Sie, dass Involvement eine Eigenschaft der *Situation* ist, nicht nur des Produkts: Ein 4-Dollar-Kaffee ist an einem Dienstag ein geringes Involvement und ein hohes Involvement, wenn Sie ihn für ein erstes Date kaufen.

segments.src: Motivation — the tension that gets you moving.**
segments.tr: Motivation — die Spannung, die Sie in Bewegung setzt.**

segments.src: Motivation is an activated need: a gap between where you are and where you want to be, strong enough to push you toward action.
segments.tr: Motivation ist ein aktiviertes Bedürfnis: eine Lücke zwischen dem Ort, an dem Sie sind, und dem, an dem Sie sein möchten, die stark genug ist, um Sie zum Handeln zu drängen.

segments.src: Two flavors usually run at once:
segments.tr: Zwei Geschmacksrichtungen laufen meistens gleichzeitig:

segments.src: - *Utilitarian* motives — solve the problem. Keep my feet from hurting. Get the laundry clean.
segments.tr: - *Utilitaristische* Motive — lösen das Problem. Verhindern, dass meine Füße schmerzen. Die Wäsche sauber bekommen.

segments.src: - *Hedonic* motives — feel something. Look like the kind of person who runs. Enjoy the unboxing.
segments.tr: - *Hedonistische* Motive — etwas fühlen. Wie die Art von Person aussehen, die läuft. Das Auspacken genießen.

segments.src: Buyers rarely admit the second one out loud, which is exactly why survey answers and actual receipts often disagree.
segments.tr: Käufer geben das zweite selten laut zu, was genau der Grund ist, warum Umfrageantworten und tatsächliche Kassenbons oft nicht übereinstimmen.

segments.src: Motives also conflict: wanting the upgrade *and* not wanting the bill (approach–avoidance) is why "0% APR for 12 months" closes so many sales — it doesn't change the price, it defuses the avoidance side.
segments.tr: Motive stehen auch im Konflikt: Das Upgrade zu wollen *und* die Rechnung nicht zu wollen (Annäherungs-Vermeidungs-Konflikt) ist der Grund, warum „0 % effektiver Jahreszins für 12 Monate“ so viele Verkäufe abschließt — es ändert nicht den Preis, es entschärft die Vermeidungsseite.

segments.src: Attitude — the stored verdict you carry around.**
segments.tr: Einstellung — das gespeicherte Urteil, das Sie mit sich herumtragen.**

segments.src: An attitude is a learned, reasonably stable tendency to respond favorably or unfavorably to something.
segments.tr: Eine Einstellung ist eine gelernte, einigermaßen stabile Tendenz, auf etwas positiv oder negativ zu reagieren.

segments.src: The classic model has three parts, often called ABC:
segments.tr: Das klassische Modell hat drei Teile, oft ABC genannt:

segments.src: - **Affect** — how you feel about it ("Patagonia feels honest")
segments.tr: - **Affekt** — wie Sie darüber denken („Patagonia fühlt sich ehrlich an“)

segments.src: - **Behavior** — what you intend to do ("I'd buy it next time")
segments.tr: - **Verhalten** — was Sie zu tun beabsichtigen („Ich würde es das nächste Mal kaufen“)

segments.src: - **Cognition** — what you believe about it ("their gear lasts a decade")
segments.tr: - **Kognition** — was Sie darüber glauben („ihre Ausrüstung hält ein Jahrzehnt“)

segments.src: A useful working model is the multiattribute view: your overall attitude is roughly the sum of what you believe about each attribute, weighted by how much that attribute matters to you.
segments.tr: Ein nützliches Arbeitsmodell ist die Multiattribut-Sicht: Ihre Gesamteinstellung ist grob die Summe dessen, was Sie über jedes Attribut glauben, gewichtet danach, wie wichtig Ihnen dieses Attribut ist.

segments.src: Attitude ≈ sum of (belief about attribute) × (importance of that attribute)
segments.tr: Attitude ≈ sum of (belief about attribute) × (importance of that attribute)

segments.src: That equation quietly explains most marketing tactics.
segments.tr: Diese Gleichung erklärt stillschweigend die meisten Marketingtaktiken.

segments.src: If people rate you low on an attribute, you can change the belief ("actually, we're 30% lighter").
segments.tr: Wenn Leute Sie bei einem Attribut schlecht bewerten, können Sie den Glauben ändern („tatsächlich sind wir 30 % leichter“).

segments.src: Or change the weight ("weight isn't what causes injuries — cushioning is").
segments.tr: Oder das Gewicht ändern („Gewicht ist nicht das, was Verletzungen verursacht — Dämpfung ist es“).

segments.src: Or add a brand-new attribute nobody was scoring yet ("carbon plate").
segments.tr: Oder ein brandneues Attribut hinzufügen, das noch niemand bewertet hat („Karbonplatte“).

segments.src: Changing what people care about is often cheaper than changing what they believe.
segments.tr: Zu ändern, worüber sich die Leute kümmern, ist oft billiger als zu ändern, was sie glauben.

segments.src: Reference groups — the invisible audience.**
segments.tr: Bezugsgruppen — das unsichtbare Publikum.**

segments.src: A reference group is any set of people you use as a benchmark for your own beliefs and behavior.
segments.tr: Eine Bezugsgruppe ist jede Gruppe von Menschen, die Sie als Maßstab für Ihre eigenen Überzeugungen und Ihr Verhalten verwenden.

segments.src: Three types matter: **membership** groups you actually belong to, **aspirational** groups you'd like to join, and **dissociative** groups you actively want to avoid resembling.
segments.tr: Drei Typen sind wichtig: **Mitgliedschafts**gruppen, denen Sie tatsächlich angehören, **Aspirations**gruppen, denen Sie gerne beitreten würden, und **dissoziative** Gruppen, denen Sie aktiv nicht ähneln wollen.

segments.src: They influence you two ways: **normative** ("buy this or you won't fit in") and **informational** ("these people know things I don't, so I'll copy them").
segments.tr: Sie beeinflussen Sie auf zwei Arten: **normativ** („kauf das, sonst passt du nicht dazu“) und **informational** („diese Leute wissen Dinge, die ich nicht weiß, also kopiere ich sie“).

segments.src: The practical rule researchers have found repeatedly: reference groups exert the most pull on things that are **publicly visible and non-essential** — the car in the driveway, the water bottle on your desk.
segments.tr: Die praktische Regel, die Forscher wiederholt gefunden haben: Bezugsgruppen üben den größten Zug auf Dinge aus, die **öffentlich sichtbar und nicht essenziell** sind — das Auto in der Einfahrt, die Wasserflasche auf Ihrem Schreibtisch.

segments.src: They exert the least pull on private necessities.
segments.tr: Sie üben den geringsten Zug auf private Notwendigkeiten aus.

segments.src: Nobody chooses a mattress to impress the neighbors.
segments.tr: Niemand wählt eine Matratze aus, um die Nachbarn zu beeindrucken.

segments.tr: Diese Überzeugungen stammten aus Werbung, von einem Arbeitskollegen und einem Podcast — nicht davon, dass Sie die Schuhe jemals getragen haben.

segments.src: Now watch the salesperson work the equation: "Everyone worries about weight, but for a first half, cushioning is what saves your knees."
segments.tr: Sehen Sie nun zu, wie der Verkäufer die Gleichung bearbeitet: „Jeder macht sich Sorgen über das Gewicht, aber für einen ersten Halbmarathon ist die Dämpfung das, was Ihre Knie schont.“

segments.src: He didn't argue with your beliefs.
segments.tr: Er hat nicht mit Ihren Überzeugungen argumentiert.

segments.src: He reweighted the attributes, and suddenly the Hokas look smart.
segments.tr: Er hat die Attribute neu gewichtet, und plötzlich sehen die Hokas schick aus.

segments.src: **Reference groups** close the deal.
segments.tr: **Bezugsgruppen** machen den Sack zu.

segments.src: The Saturday morning run club you just joined is a membership group — you notice half of them wear the same shoe and you feel the pull to match (normative), and you also assume they know things you don't (informational).
segments.tr: Der Samstagmorgen-Laufclub, dem Sie gerade beigetreten sind, ist eine Mitgliedschaftsgruppe — Sie bemerken, dass die Hälfte von ihnen denselben Schuh trägt, und Sie spüren den Drang, sich anzupassen (normativ), und Sie nehmen auch an, dass sie Dinge wissen, die Sie nicht wissen (informational).

segments.src: The guy who ran Boston is your aspirational group; the Strava thread is a running commentary of both.
segments.tr: Der Typ, der Boston gelaufen ist, ist Ihre Aspirationsgruppe; der Strava-Thread ist ein laufender Kommentar von beiden.

segments.src: And the shoes are highly visible and entirely optional — the exact conditions where reference group influence is strongest.
segments.tr: Und die Schuhe sind hochsichtbar und völlig optional — genau die Bedingungen, unter denen der Einfluss der Bezugsgruppe am stärksten ist.

segments.src: Your mattress, bought last spring, got none of this energy at all.
segments.tr: Ihre Matratze, die letzten Frühling gekauft wurde, hat all diese Energie überhaupt nicht abbekommen.

segments.src: ## Three-Line Recap
segments.tr: ## Zusammenfassung in drei Zeilen

segments.src: 1. **Involvement** decides how much thinking a purchase gets — driven by perceived risk (money, visibility, permanence), and it's situational, not just product-based.
segments.tr: 1. **Involvement** entscheidet, wie viel Nachdenken ein Kauf erhält — angetrieben durch wahrgenommenes Risiko (Geld, Sichtbarkeit, Dauerhaftigkeit), und es ist situationsbedingt, nicht nur produktbasiert.

segments.src: 2. **Motivation** is the activated need pushing you forward, and it's usually utilitarian and hedonic at once; **attitude** is your stored verdict, roughly beliefs weighted by importance — which is why reweighting attributes is a marketer's cheapest lever.
segments.tr: 2. **Motivation** ist das aktivierte Bedürfnis, das Sie vorwärts treibt, und es ist normalerweise gleichzeitig utilitaristisch und hedonistisch; **Einstellung** ist Ihr gespeichertes Urteil, grob gesagt Überzeugungen, gewichtet nach Wichtigkeit — weshalb das Neuwiegen von Attributen der billigste Hebel eines Vermarkters ist.

segments.src: 3. **Reference groups** shape choices most powerfully when the product is publicly visible and non-essential, through normative (fit in) and informational (they know better) influence.
segments.tr: 3. **Bezugsgruppen** formen Entscheidungen am stärksten, wenn das Produkt öffentlich sichtbar und nicht essenziell ist, durch normativen (dazugehören) und informationalen (sie wissen es besser) Einfluss.

segments.tr: ## ✅ Selbsttest
